comments.text: Having a personality disorder doesn’t necessarily make anyone a killer, but if you’re having trouble with your impulsive behavior,and have issues with loosing control, then you should at least consider going to a therapist to try to get some help. The ones who have antisocial personality disorder and the ones who have Narcissistic personality disorder are often the ones who never actually attempt to get help , because they don’t think there’s anything wrong with their behavior. They will often blame everyone else for their own failures. I’ve got Borderline personality disorder, and was diagnosed at 18 years of age, because I started having problems at 17, and I felt awful about the way my mental illness affected my family who I was still living with. I was terrified for many years that my obvious lack of impulsivity would seriously harm others, because I had so much anger pent up inside, and that scared me even more. So I’ve been going to several different kinds of therapy, and the last ( and best) psychiatrist I’ve been seeing for almost 20 years now.  He’s never given up on me, no matter how serious I harmed myself, and despite what other doctors would say about me. I wouldn’t be alive if it wasn’t for him . He made me heal from the SA trauma that I was dealing with as a child, from one of my parents neighbors. The trauma is probably what caused me to get the Borderline Personality Disorder in the first place. Having had BPD for almost 4 decades has been intensively painful, it’s an horrible pain to be dealing with. When you know what your issues are and you’re young, like in your teens and during the 20’s , there are also a lot of things going on in your body’s- hormones and being pre-menstrual can really mess with your brain as well as the lower regions of your body. I found out that the 20’s and early thirties were the most unstable times of my life. When I was around 35 life became easier to deal with. I went through anger management, which shaved off a lot of my «sharp « edges. Being a person who loved being around animals like horses, I felt strongly towards people who were mean to animals. And I didn’t like authorities very well either, because I’ve  always hated racism, zionism , unfairness etc and unfortunately a lot of the authorities represented all of that, and they still do that to this day.But I learned how to stay as much as possible away from any confrontational situations, because I knew that would put me on edge and I was scared of what the consequences of that might be. Even though I’m still in therapy, I ‘m much calmer and more content about life than I ever thought possible. A lot of psychologists and psychiatrists never wanted to have me as a client, so for years and years I was seen by a multitude of different therapist, all in all 35 different individuals. The last death is only 1 year ago, so it’s an endless sea of grief that you’re kind of waddling around in. It never gets any easier either.
